findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The backup probe thermometer is stored in a pan mixed in with scrapers used for the chicken baking equipment. This poses a possible contamination source for the food contact parts of the probe thermometer and this practice should cease moving forward. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they had the probe sanitized and moved to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they remain clean/sanitized prior to use.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple knives are being stored between the knife rack and the wall. The wall is visibly discolored and possibly soiled around the knife rack and behind it. This is not a clean location for food contact surfaces to be in contact with while in storage. The PIC was shown and tthe situation discussed. The knives were move to dish for re-cleaning and should not be stored here moving forward. Ensure all food contact surfaces are stored in a clean location after cleaning and before use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to change gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted to correct and the PIC is instructed to ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

Multiple trays of cleaned utensils are stored in plastic tubs on shelves in the kitchen area. These tubs are observed with standing water and a slimy substance in them that is in contact with the utensils. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. The utensils were moved to dish for re-cleaning and the tubs replaced during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all cleaned utensils are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times until use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The floor under shelves on both sides of the walk in cooler are in need of mopping. 2) The wall near the floor in the walk in cooler appears to have mold growth developing. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

The hand sink to the far right in the deli area (behind the end display cooler) is observed without hand soap during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and a new container installed during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The open top cooler on the deli floor has numerous packages of meat and cheese with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-48F. All items of concern were discarded during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The open top cooler on the floor is not holding meats and cheeses at sufficient temperature for safety. The items noted out of temperature have been discarded, but the cooler needs to be brought into compliance. Follow up in 2 weeks to ensure the equipment is properly functioning.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Multiple employees are observed to either change gloves or put on gloves without hand washing. Education conducted and the PIC should ensure that safe hand washing practices are taking place in the food handler/ preparation areas.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Multiple items in the island cooler observed with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-48F. Items include calzones, sandwiches, salads and subs. Through investigation it appears that any foods on the bottom shelf should not be stacked more than 2 high. Also, items on the ends should be placed so that air may flow from the back of the cooler and effectively maintain the front layer of foods in safe temperatures. Foods in these areas as well as the ones probed were discarded to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the customer display reach in cooler observed out of temperature. Shredded rotisserie pork observed at 50F. Product was stacked 4 containers high in the bottom of the cooler. Packages lower (closer to the bottom) were observed at 41F or below. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC and staff. Employee removed top layer and checked internal temperature of remaining packages. Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Review stocking procedures with all staff so that product is not stacked too high.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Three containers of sushi observed labeled use by 6/7. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Out of date foods removed from sale to be voluntarily discarded. PIC instructed employees to check the whole cooler for expired foods.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Sandwiches in the island cooler observed to be 45 to 50F. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Sandwiches removed to be rapidly chilled or voluntarily discarded. Sandwiches appeared to be stocked too far to the front of the cooler, preventing them from being kept at 41F or below. Food closer to the back of the shelves observed 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Red buckets under the slicers observed with 0ppm quat. CORRECTED- Bucket was emptied and refilled from the wall-mounted dispenser to the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label. (Pf)

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
Time as a control is used on hot foods for service (mac & cheese, mashed potatoes, various chickens, etc). All items were observed without time markings indicating when they were removed from temperature control or when they were to be discarded. CORRECTED— Foods were observed to be 135F or above. Staff were confident that foods were removed from temperature control at 1:30, and labeled items accordingly.
3-501.19: (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P)

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Knives observed stored in the gap between the knife rack and the wall. CORRECTED-- Knives removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Knives will be stored in a clean location.
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.
